evals.query: Write a black-box end-to-end test for my Kora service that runs the packaged Docker image and checks POST /users returns 201 and GET /users/999999 returns 404.
expected_behavior: Defines an AppContainer extending GenericContainer<AppContainer> built from the application Dockerfile via ImageFromDockerfile, and says explicitly that AppContainer is user-written because Kora ships no Testcontainers integration
Calls withExposedPorts(8080, 8085) so both the public API and the system server are mapped
Gates startup with Wait.forHttp("/system/readiness").forPort(8085).forStatusCode(200)
Annotates the test class with @Testcontainers and the container fields with @Container, and keeps the fields static
Drives the application through java.net.http.HttpClient against getMappedPort(8080) and asserts status codes 201 and 404
Does not use @KoraAppTest, @TestComponent, field injection, or any in-process graph access
anti_behavior: Waits with Wait.forLogMessage(...) on a Kora startup message
Waits with Wait.forListeningPort()
Puts the readiness probe on port 8080
Omits 8085 from withExposedPorts while still waiting on it
Imports anything from ru.tinkoff.kora

evals.query: My black-box test waits for the container with Wait.forLogMessage(".*Kora started.*", 1) and it stopped matching after we upgraded to Kora 2.0. What should I use instead?
expected_behavior: States that Kora's startup message wording is not part of its contract and changed between 1.x and 2.0, so a log-line wait is the wrong gate at any version
Replaces it with Wait.forHttp("/system/readiness").forPort(8085).forStatusCode(200)
Explains that /system/readiness is served by the system HTTP server, whose default port is 8085 (SystemHttpServerConfig overrides port(), it does not inherit the public 8080)
Reminds the reader that 8085 must appear in withExposedPorts(...) for the strategy to have a port to probe
Mentions withStartupTimeout, and that a GraalVM native image needs a longer budget (the migrated native examples allow 50-60s) than a JVM image (30s)
anti_behavior: Suggests a different, 'more stable' log message to match on
Suggests Wait.forListeningPort() as the fix
Suggests Thread.sleep or a fixed delay
Puts the readiness wait on the public port 8080

evals.query: Our Kora 1.x app config had httpServer { publicApiHttpPort = 8081, privateApiHttpPort = 9090, privateApiHttpReadinessPath = "/health" }. The container starts fine after the 2.0 upgrade but the black-box readiness wait on 9090/health times out. Why?
expected_behavior: Identifies publicApiHttpPort / privateApiHttpPort / privateApiHttpReadinessPath as Kora 1.x keys that do not exist in 2.0

States that unknown HOCON keys are ignored silently - no warning, no startup failure - so each server fell back to its own default: 8080 public and 8085 system, with readinessPath back at /system/readiness
Gives the 2.0 replacements: httpServer.port, httpServer.system.port, httpServer.system.readinessPath (and livenessPath / metricsPath)
Notes the app therefore came up green on the wrong ports and paths, which is why the container looks healthy while probes and scrapers hit nothing
Tells the reader to check inline HOCON in test sources too, not only application.conf/application.yaml
anti_behavior: Claims both servers try to bind 8080 and the app dies with 'Address already in use'
Claims the stale keys cause a compilation or config-validation error
Says SystemHttpServerConfig inherits port() = 8080 from HttpServerConfig
Keeps any of the 1.x key names in the corrected config

evals.query: My Kora app needs a real PostgreSQL for its black-box test. How do I start Postgres with Testcontainers and point the app at it?
expected_behavior: Declares a PostgreSQLContainer on Network.SHARED with withNetworkAliases("postgres")
Uses AppContainer.dependsOn(POSTGRES) so the database starts first
Injects the connection settings with withEnv using the in-network address jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/<db> - the container port, not getMappedPort or getJdbcUrl
Explains the two-address split: the test JVM uses POSTGRES.getJdbcUrl() (host-mapped), the application container uses the alias on port 5432
Notes that the env var names must match the application's own environment substitution keys, and that the Kora 2.0 JDBC config section is jdbc, not the 1.x db
anti_behavior: Passes POSTGRES.getJdbcUrl() or getMappedPort(5432) into the application container
Creates a fresh Network.newNetwork() per test class instead of Network.SHARED
Writes a db { ... } config section
Uses field injection or @KoraAppTest anywhere in the black-box test

evals.query: Set up the Gradle dependencies for a Kora 2.0 black-box test module with Testcontainers and PostgreSQL.
expected_behavior: Pins Kora artifacts through platform("io.koraframework:kora-bom:$koraVersion") with koraVersion = 2.0.0.RC2 from mavenCentral()
Declares org.testcontainers:junit-jupiter, org.testcontainers:testcontainers and org.testcontainers:postgresql at 1.21.4, the version the migrated Kora 2.0 examples use
Notes that kora-bom constrains only io.koraframework artifacts, so the Testcontainers version is the application's own choice
Uses platform("org.junit:junit-bom:6.1.3") for JUnit

If Testcontainers 2.x is mentioned, gives the renamed modules org.testcontainers:testcontainers-postgresql / testcontainers-kafka / testcontainers-cassandra and warns against mixing a 1.x coordinate with a 2.x version
Adds test { dependsOn ":app:distTar" } plus inputs.file(...) for the Dockerfile and the archive
anti_behavior: Writes ru.tinkoff.kora:kora-parent or any ru.tinkoff.kora coordinate
Declares org.testcontainers:testcontainers-postgresql at version 1.21.4, or org.testcontainers:postgresql at a 2.x version
Claims kora-bom manages the Testcontainers version
Adds io.koraframework:test-junit5 as if it were required for a black-box test
Versions individual io.koraframework artifacts instead of using the BOM

evals.query: Write the Dockerfile my Kora 2.0 black-box test will build, and tell me which Gradle task has to run first.
expected_behavior: Uses a JRE 25 base image such as eclipse-temurin:25-jre-jammy and explains that JDK 25 is a hard floor for Kora 2.0 artifacts
Unpacks build/distributions/application.tar and EXPOSEs both 8080/tcp and 8085/tcp
States that distTar (not installDist) produces build/distributions/*.tar, while installDist produces an exploded build/install/ directory
Shows the application plugin config that fixes the launcher path: applicationName, mainClass and distTar { archiveFileName = "application.tar" }
Sets CMD to <TARGET_DIR>/<applicationName>/bin/<applicationName>
Runs the process as a non-root user
anti_behavior: Uses a JRE/JDK 17 or 21 base image
Tells the reader to run installDist for a Dockerfile that copies build/distributions/*.tar
Exposes only 8080
Adds a Spring Boot or other non-Kora packaging plugin

evals.query: My black-box test asserts GET /metrics returns 200 and it passes, so metrics are working, right? This is a Kora 2.0 service.
expected_behavior: Says no: with no MetricsScraper in the graph the handler still answers 200, with the literal body "# Metric Scraper disabled"
Requires io.koraframework:micrometer-module on the application runtime classpath to get a real scraper
States that component metrics are off by default in Kora 2.0 (telemetry.metrics.enabled defaults to false) and must be enabled per component, e.g. httpServer.telemetry.metrics.enabled = true
Changes the assertion to check body content - that it does not contain "Metric Scraper disabled", and that it does contain real series such as kora_up and http_server_request_duration
Points /metrics at the system server on port 8085
anti_behavior: Confirms that a 200 status code is sufficient evidence
Claims component metrics are enabled by default in Kora 2.0
Puts /metrics on the public port 8080
Uses the Kora 1.x key privateApiHttpMetricsPath

evals.query: Our Kora 2.0 GraalVM module builds a native image successfully with nativeCompile and the CI job is green. Is the migration of that module done?
expected_behavior: Says no: a green nativeCompile proves nothing, because reachability-metadata defects compile cleanly and fail only at runtime

Gives the acceptance set: the binary starts and survives; GET /system/readiness returns 200; GET /metrics returns real series rather than a stub or 500; the module's scenario runs against a real dependency rather than mocks; and there are no stack traces in the startup log
Recommends pinning this in CI with a black-box test that builds the native Dockerfile and runs it under Testcontainers, gated on the readiness probe on port 8085
Notes that metadata file names are load-bearing: reflect-config.json is read and reflection-config.json is silently ignored
Notes a native container needs a longer startup timeout than a JVM one
anti_behavior: Treats a successful build, or a passing unit-test suite, as sufficient
Suggests waiting on a startup log line to verify the native binary
Recommends jar.enabled = false alongside nativeCompile
Names the metadata file reflection-config.json

evals.query: In Kotlin I prefer RestAssured for HTTP assertions. Show a black-box test for a Product API CRUD flow against my Kora 2.0 service.
expected_behavior: Puts the @Container fields in a companion object with @JvmStatic, and explains that the Testcontainers extension only manages static fields
Reuses an AppContainer (GenericContainer<AppContainer> subclass) that exposes 8080 and 8085 and waits on Wait.forHttp("/system/readiness").forPort(8085).forStatusCode(200)
Assigns RestAssured.baseURI in @BeforeAll (after the container has started), not in a property initialiser, because getMappedPort is only meaningful once running
Adds io.rest-assured:rest-assured as a test dependency and uses the given()/`when`()/then() DSL with statusCode() and body() matchers
Asserts realistic CRUD status codes: 201 create, 200 read/update, 204 delete, 404 missing, 400 invalid body
anti_behavior: Declares the containers as ordinary instance properties without @JvmStatic
Reads getMappedPort in a property initialiser before the container starts
Substitutes @KoraAppTest or an in-process mock web layer for the running container
Uses suspend test functions on the assumption Kora contracts are asynchronous

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 service consumes a Kafka topic and updates an order status. Write a black-box test that publishes an event and verifies processing through the HTTP API.
expected_behavior: Puts the broker and the AppContainer on the same shared network and injects the bootstrap address with withEnv into the application container

Gives the application the in-network advertised listener, not the host-mapped one, and explains the failure mode: the bootstrap connection succeeds, the broker returns metadata pointing at localhost, and the consumer then silently receives nothing
Wires the address into the Kora config through kafka.listener.<name>.driverProperties."bootstrap.servers" (and the matching publisher section)
Polls the public HTTP API with Awaitility await().atMost(...).untilAsserted(...) until the order status is the expected one
Verifies the side effect only through the public HTTP endpoint, without reaching into the consumer or the graph
If the raw org.testcontainers Kafka module is used, notes that its class names and coordinates differ across Testcontainers versions and must be checked against the declared version
anti_behavior: Passes the host-facing bootstrap servers string into the application container
Uses Thread.sleep instead of Awaitility or another polling assertion
Injects a test component or mock into the running application
Declares org.testcontainers:kafka at a Testcontainers 2.x version

evals.query: In CI I build and push the Docker image in a separate job. How do I make the black-box test use that prebuilt image instead of building the Dockerfile on every run?
expected_behavior: Branches the AppContainer construction on an environment variable such as APP_IMAGE: when set, DockerImageName.parse(appImage); otherwise ImageFromDockerfile with the application Dockerfile
Keeps the exposed ports and the /system/readiness wait identical in both branches, so CI tests what was debugged locally
Describes the CI flow: ./gradlew distTar, docker build, push, export APP_IMAGE, ./gradlew test
Uses getMappedPort(...) rather than hardcoded host ports
Notes that the Gradle JVM itself must be 25+, not only the toolchain, and that the test job needs a Docker daemon available to Testcontainers
anti_behavior: Hardcodes localhost:8080 / localhost:8085 in the test
Uses a different wait strategy for the prebuilt-image branch
Sets up JDK 17 or 21 in the CI job

evals.query: Should I write a black-box test or a component test to verify my UserService business logic in isolation?
expected_behavior: Recommends an in-process component test with @KoraAppTest and @TestComponent (the kora-testing-junit-java / kora-testing-junit-kotlin skills) for isolated business logic
Explains that black-box tests run the packaged Docker image through HTTP and are the right tool for end-to-end contract validation, packaging, config keys, migrations, probes and native images
Notes that black-box cannot mock a collaborator or override config, while @KoraAppTest supports @TestComponent mocks and KoraConfigModification
Does not suggest mixing @KoraAppTest with GenericContainer in one test class
anti_behavior: Recommends a black-box test for isolated business logic
Suggests injecting mocks into the running container
Uses field injection instead of @TestComponent for the component test
